description: Reviewed first-stage gates for semantic operations not yet covered by the dedicated ambiguity and duplicate campaigns. SHORT cases establish the bounded label contract; LONG cases begin Task 1-3 scaling without claiming full-operation parity.

conflict.instruction: Return YES only when both statements govern the same scope and cannot both hold. Return MAY when an unresolved ordinary referent or scope choice determines whether they conflict: if an underspecified phrase can ordinarily denote either of two explicit candidates, do not silently choose the most likely candidate. Return NO only when the available text fixes compatible scopes.

atomize.instruction: Return COMPOSITE when the source contains independently revisable commitments that can be split while preserving their conditions; ATOMIC when it expresses one commitment even if long; UNRESOLVED when missing structure prevents a safe boundary decision.

translate.instruction: Compare source and translation. PRESERVED retains proposition, scope, modality, conditions, and exceptions; LOSSY omits or weakens material; CONTRADICTED reverses or incompatibly changes it; UNKNOWN is reserved for an unresolved source meaning.

compare.instruction: Classify two Memories: EQUIVALENT if mutually substitutable, COMPATIBLE if jointly useful on one topic, CONFLICT if incompatible in the same scope, DISTINCT if independently about different predicates, and UNKNOWN only when an unresolved referent controls the result.

update.instruction: Classify one verified source against the supplied target candidate: ALREADY_PRESENT for full semantic presence, EDIT for a same-subject replacement or refinement, ADD for a new independently useful fact, REMOVE only for an explicit whole-target retirement, and UNRESOLVED when authority or target identity is insufficient.

ground.instruction: Classify one independently reviewable dialogue unit by its durable role: RULE constrains future behavior, FACT asserts world state, MEMORY is an input-output example, GOAL states the desired outcome, and QUESTION requests missing information.

meld.instruction: Classify one cross-Context relation before proposing any meld: EQUIVALENT for mutual substitution, COMPATIBLE for information that can coexist and combine, CONFLICT for incompatible same-scope commitments, DISTINCT for unrelated independent content, UNKNOWN for unresolved scope.

forget.instruction: Given a forget request and one Memory, REMOVE when the whole Memory is in scope, EDIT when only part is in scope and the remainder is independently meaningful, otherwise KEEP.

integrate.instruction: Given new information and one candidate Memory, NO_CHANGE means already present, EDIT means the same independently revisable subject should be refined or superseded, ADD means the new proposition is independent, and UNRESOLVED means the relation cannot safely be decided.

cases.scenario: Same proposal and same primary-method scope.

input.left: Use a controlled usability study as the primary evaluation.
input.right: Do not use a controlled usability study as the primary evaluation; use field deployment instead.

expected.label: YES
expected.rationale: The directives select incompatible primary methods in the same scope.

cases.scenario: The building has a main entrance and a separate staff entrance.

input.left: The main entrance closes after 5 p.m.
input.right: Staff may use the entrance after 5 p.m.

expected.label: MAY
expected.rationale: The unspecified entrance controls whether the permissions collide.

cases.scenario: Two distinct entrances are explicit.

input.left: The main entrance closes after 5 p.m.
input.right: The staff entrance remains open after 5 p.m.

expected.label: NO
expected.rationale: Different entrances can have different access rules.

cases.scenario: The same facility has explicit non-overlapping time scopes.

input.left: The main entrance is closed after 5 p.m. on weekdays.
input.right: The main entrance remains open after 5 p.m. on weekends.

expected.label: NO
expected.rationale: Weekday and weekend rules have different explicit time scopes and can coexist.

cases.scenario: Two equal-authority advisors discuss one HCI proposal. Background text describes interviews, a prototype, recruitment limits, ethics review, and a two-page submission, but only the primary research-question form is being compared.

input.left: Advisor 1: Keep the exploratory interview work, but formulate the primary research question as a directional quantitative hypothesis so the main contribution can be tested with predefined measures. Secondary qualitative questions may explain unexpected behavior.
input.right: Advisor 2: Keep the same exploratory interview work, but formulate the primary research question as an open qualitative question because the relevant user practices are not yet understood. Do not make a directional quantitative hypothesis the primary question.

expected.label: YES
expected.rationale: Despite surrounding compatible details, the two directives oppose each other on the same primary-question slot.

cases.scenario: Two access states can change independently.

input.source: 차량 출입은 금지되고 보행자 출입문은 열려 있다.

expected.label: COMPOSITE
expected.rationale: Vehicle and pedestrian access are independently revisable.

cases.scenario: Conditions jointly scope one action.

expected.label: ATOMIC
expected.rationale: All modifiers define one contact rule.

cases.scenario: The source is a damaged fragment.

expected.label: UNRESOLVED
expected.rationale: The fragment does not expose stable proposition boundaries.

cases.scenario: A personal sharing guardrail contains one conditional decision rule plus explanatory context.

input.source: 정부 의료기관의 요청이 가족 연락처와 최근 진료 일정을 함께 요구하더라도, 사용자가 이 특정 요청에 대해 두 범주의 전송을 각각 승인하지 않았다면 에이전트는 어느 범주도 전송하지 말고, 필요한 이유와 보관 기간을 먼저 질문한 뒤 사용자가 범주별로 선택할 수 있게 해야 한다.

expected.label: ATOMIC
expected.rationale: The prohibition, question, and choice are coupled steps of one conditional disclosure rule, not independent timeless facts.

cases.scenario: A reviewed Korean-English pair.

input.translation: The main entrance closes at 5 p.m.

expected.label: PRESERVED
expected.rationale: Place, action, and time are retained.

input.source: 정문은 오후 5시에 닫히지만 교직원 출입은 허용된다.
input.translation: The main entrance closes at 5 p.m.

expected.label: LOSSY
expected.rationale: The staff exception was omitted.

input.translation: Visitors must use the south entrance.

expected.label: CONTRADICTED
expected.rationale: A prohibition became an obligation.

cases.scenario: Task 1 accessibility guidance with conditions and an uncertainty boundary.

input.source: 공사 기간에는 3층 후문에서 도서관으로 이어지는 accessible route를 이용할 수 없다. 학생이 그 경로를 이용하려고 하면 먼저 폐쇄 사실을 알리고, 확인된 대체 경로가 있을 때에만 그 경로를 안내하라. 현장 문 잠금 상태는 실시간으로 보증하지 마라.
input.translation: During construction, the accessible route from the third-floor rear entrance to the library is unavailable. If a student plans to use it, first explain the closure and suggest an alternative only when that route has been verified. Do not guarantee the door's real-time lock state.

expected.label: PRESERVED
expected.rationale: The closure, ordering, verification condition, and observation limit are all retained.

cases.scenario: Same advice in different wording.

input.left: Recruit participants who match the target user group.
input.right: Participant recruitment should reflect the intended users.

expected.label: EQUIVALENT
expected.rationale: Each can substitute for the other at this scope.

cases.scenario: Two pieces complete one methods section.

input.right: Explain how interview data will be analyzed.

expected.label: COMPATIBLE
expected.rationale: The requirements differ but jointly contribute to the same methods plan.

cases.scenario: Independent personal facts.

input.right: The spare key is kept by the user's aunt.

expected.label: DISTINCT
expected.rationale: The predicates are independently revisable and unrelated.

cases.scenario: The proposal has a strict page limit. Compare the substantive advice, not style.

input.left: Use the first paragraph of the methods section to name the target users, recruitment channel, sample rationale, prototype task, and the observations that answer the research question. Put foreseeable recruitment limitations beside the sampling decision.
input.right: Within the methods section, make the chain from target population through recruitment and prototype tasks to the evidence used for the research question explicit. Discuss sampling limitations where readers can evaluate the recruitment choice.

expected.label: EQUIVALENT
expected.rationale: The second restates the same required chain and placement without losing an operational requirement.

cases.scenario: A verified construction bulletin and one existing wiki Memory are compared. The bulletin also contains provenance wording that must not become the target content.

cases.scenario: Classify the independently selected unit between markers; surrounding transcript is context only.

input.transcript: User: I may share appointment dates, but I am not agreeing to share diagnoses. Agent: I understand that the categories require separate review. User: Also show me the exact recipient before anything is sent.
input.selected_unit: Before any transfer, show the user the exact recipient and require approval for that recipient.

expected.label: RULE
expected.rationale: The selected unit is a reusable behavioral constraint, not a claim that transfer occurred.

cases.scenario: One source adds cause to a target state.

input.left: The garage is closed during construction.
input.right: Waterproofing work is underway in the garage.

expected.label: COMPATIBLE
expected.rationale: The state and cause can coexist and be combined without contradiction.

cases.scenario: Two advisor Contexts use different structure but equal authority. The selected units concern evaluation evidence only.

input.left: Use a controlled usability study to estimate task success, completion time, and recurring interaction failures under repeatable prototype conditions. Follow it with brief interviews to explain the observed breakdowns.
input.right: Collect repeatable task-performance measures with the prototype, including success and completion time, and use post-task interviews to interpret why the observed interaction failures occurred.

expected.label: EQUIVALENT
expected.rationale: Both specify the same primary evidence and explanatory follow-up despite different wording.

cases.scenario: The request covers the whole Memory.

input.memory: My dental appointment is Friday at 2 p.m.

expected.label: REMOVE
expected.rationale: Every proposition concerns the requested appointment.

cases.scenario: Only one clause is in scope.

input.memory: My dental appointment is Friday, and my aunt keeps the spare key.

expected.label: EDIT
expected.rationale: The unrelated spare-key fact remains meaningful.

cases.scenario: No semantic match.

expected.label: KEEP
expected.rationale: The Memory is outside the request.

cases.scenario: A personal Memory joins an appointment detail with an independently useful communication preference and a dependent reason.

input.request: Forget all details of my October cardiology appointment, including its preparation instructions.
input.memory: The October 18 cardiology appointment is at 9:30 a.m., and the clinic asked me to avoid food after midnight. Because phone calls about medical scheduling are stressful, I generally prefer appointment changes by text message.

expected.label: EDIT
expected.rationale: The appointment and preparation details are removed, while the general communication preference remains independently useful.

cases.scenario: New construction guidance has the same facility and period as an existing Memory but introduces an independently useful route rather than replacing the facility state.

input.new_info: While the Main Building accessible ramp is closed during construction, visitors who need step-free access can use the temporary accessible route from the south entrance through the library foyer; staff should explain the turn before the security desk.
input.memory: The Main Building accessible ramp is closed during construction.
